title: Rapid POC constraints matrix + success checklist
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact kickoff + acceptance checklist for the Catalyst customer POC (contact: product@catalyst.ai). It is intentionally terse so customers + SEs can iterate quickly during week 0 and the workshop. Focus: demonstrate a single production-oriented flow (hosted API -> model variant -> integrated client) and capture quantitative pass/fail gates for go/no-go.

High-level objective:
- Validate inference economics and latency at representative QPS (10 sustained RPS, 50 peak RPS) with model X-7B (quantized) under realistic prompt mix.
- Confirm end-to-end integration for private deployment option (VPC peering) and a canary fallback to hosted API.

Quick roles (who does what):
- Customer lead: Maya Singh (Catalyst)
- SE Lead / POC owner: Avery Chen (redwood)
- Infra / Oncall: Liam O'Connor
- Eval & Quality: Samira Patel
- Security / Compliance: Priya Rao
- Exec sponsor (customer): Ravi Kumar

Week 0 workshop agenda (90min):
- 0-10m: Introductions + constraints overview (SE lead)
- 10-25m: Customer workload walk-through (customer) - 3 representative flows + latency expectations
- 25-45m: Proposed architecture (SE) - hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
- 45-65m: Acceptance gates & metrics (joint) - agree on datasets, thresholds, and evaluation cadence
- 65-80m: Deployment timeline + responsibilities (ops)
- 80-90m: Open issues & parking lot (all)

Constraints matrix (fill during workshop):
- Data residency: (required) e.g., customer data must not leave eu-west-1 -> OK for Dedicated / Private, hosted needs explicit approval
- Max acceptable p95 lat: (ms) - target and hard SLO
- Cost constraint: monthly inference spend target (USD)
- Throughput: sustained RPS / burst size
- Input size: average and 95th token length
- Eval pass-rate: % of outputs that match golden-label acceptance heuristics
- Security: KMS/HSM required? audit logs retention days

Example filled row (sample):
- Data residency: eu-west-1 only
- p95 latency: <= 350ms (target), <= 500ms (hard stop)
- Cost: <= $2k/month for steady-state (proof calculation attached separately)
- Throughput: 10 RPS sustained, 50 RPS burst for 15s
- Input size: avg 120 tokens, 95th 620 tokens
- Eval pass-rate: >= 88% on 300 eval prompts
- Security: KMS with customer CMKs, audit logs 90d

Success checklist (quantitative gates) - all must be met for formal acceptance unless specifically marked as "conditional":
1) Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for the live workload at sustained load (10 RPS) - gate
2) Throughput: system can sustain 10 RPS for 1 hour without error rate > 1% - gate
3) Cost baseline: projected monthly inference cost (tokens * unit cost) within agreed budget +/- 15% - conditional (customer may accept higher cost for short demo)
4) Quality: automated eval on 300 customer-supplied prompts meets >= 88% pass (semantic similarity + business-rule checks) - gate
5) Integration: private deployment (VPC peering) completes and API endpoint accessible from customer infra with TLS + client certs - gate
6) Observability: request tracing and token-level cost breakdown are visible in console and routed to the customer's Splunk/Datadog instance - gate
7) Rollback & fallback: canary rollout to private must be configured with automatic fallback to hosted API in < 30s of error spike - gate
8) Security: KMS integration validated, secrets never logged in plane, audit events generated - gate

Acceptance test plan (short):
- Load harness: run 10 RPS steady for 60m, with 3x 15s bursts at 50 RPS. Metrics: latency histogram, error rate, GPU utilization, batch sizes, token throughput.
- Eval harness: run 300 curated prompts (provided by customer). Measure semantic threshold using embedding-similarity (>= 0.88) and business-rule pass.
- Regression harness: run baseline of 200 prompts used for internal benchmark; compare to model variant baseline for drift (>5% degradation triggers rollback).

Deployment notes (hosted vs private):
- Hosted (quick path): provision API key, set model variant to X-7B-q4 while enabling prefix caching for common templates, run initial smoke tests.
- Dedicated: reserve 2x A10-equivalent nodes (config suggested) with autoscale off for deterministic cost; prod config later.
- Private: VPC peering + route table changes (customer network team), customer provides CIDR allowlist, KMS CMK ARN, and JIT VPN window.

Operational runbook (week 1):
- Day 0 (kickoff): create test account, upload 300 eval prompts to S3, set up Prometheus + Datadog dashboards (SE + SRE)
- Day 1: baseline runs (latency + eval); capture token-level cost report
- Day 2-3: iterate prompt engineering for top 20 failure cases (eval team + customer SME)
- Day 4: private deployment smoke test and canary path validation
- Day 5: formal handover demo and sign-off meeting (customer + SE + SRE)

Risk log (top items):
- Network: VPC peering delays (mitigation: reserve a 2 hour window with network team and test route early)
- Prompts: golden labels mismatch (mitigation: define tolerance and review 30 borderline cases together)
- Cost overshoot during heavy bursts (mitigation: throttle policy + budget alert, pre-approve burst windows)
- Model quality regression after quantization (mitigation: run regression harness and have a fallback unquantized variant available)

Open questions to resolve in week 0: (assign during workshop)
- Final list of sensitive fields that must be redacted before upload? (Customer)
- Can customer accept hosted routing for first 48h if private peering not ready? (Security)
- Which region(s) must be used for data residency? (Customer)

Sign-off flow (mini):
- SE completes post-POC report with metrics -> share to customer + tech sponsor -> customer ops runs independent validation harness (48h) -> final acceptance meeting -> sign-off note + close ticket JIRA ENGPOC-789.

Parking lot / notes to self:
- Draft a short one-pager for finance explaining cost model used in the POC (who pays what for extra burst) - assign to Avery
- Prepare a short troubleshooting checklist for the customer to run if endpoint returns 5xx (include curl + example payload) - assign to Liam

Attachments & artifacts (where to put outputs):
- eval prompts: s3://redwood-poc-artifacts/catalyst/inputs-2025-01-20
- load scripts: GitHub PR 456 (serving-runtime)/workloads/catalyst-load
- post-run dashboards: Datadog link (will be attached after run)

Quick decisions logged here (workshop outcomes):
- Agreed latency gate: p95 <= 350ms (customer comfortable with 350ms for pilot)
- Customer will provide 300 eval prompts by 2025-01-22
- Private peering scheduled for 2025-01-28 (network window confirmed)

Next steps (immediate):
- SE: finalize small config JSON for the hosted canary and share with customer (Avery) - due 2025-01-17
- Customer: share redaction list and eval prompts - due 2025-01-22
- Infra: reserve dedicated nodes and create initial billing estimate - due 2025-01-21

Notes style: rough, iterative. Use this doc in the workshop, update live. If anything critical changes, update JIRA ENGPOC-789 and ping #poc-catalyst on Slack.
